title: Booking Models, Substance and Local Control
summary: How groups decide where business is originated, executed, booked and risk-managed, and how to demonstrate that the licensed entity has real substance and control over the risks on its books.
contentGaps: Written as part of a programme: Aim and Purpose is the module's one-line description; audience, prior knowledge and core reading come from the programme

sections.Aim and Purpose: How groups decide where business is originated, executed, booked and risk-managed, and how to demonstrate that the licensed entity has real substance and control over the risks on its books.
Learning Objectives: Explain common booking and remote-booking models and the risks they create
Assess whether the local entity has adequate people, decision-making and risk management on the ground
Prepare the evidence of substance that host supervisors expect
Syllabus: Origination, execution, booking and risk management across entities
Back-to-back and remote booking: transfer of risk and its limits
Substance tests: senior people, decision-making, controls and records
Red flags supervisors look for in empty or letterbox entities
Intended Audience: Chairs, executive, non-executive and independent directors of regulated subsidiaries, and of parent and holding companies
Country heads, branch managers and senior managers responsible for a local entity within a wider group
Group and local heads of compliance, risk, legal, governance and regulatory affairs
sections.Useful Prior Knowledge and Experience: Board, senior management or control function experience in a firm that is part of a group or operates across borders is helpful. No legal background is required.
Core Reading: FSB, Enhancing Third-Party Risk Management and Oversight: A Toolkit for Financial Institutions and Financial Authorities (2023)
Basel Committee, Principles for Effective Supervisory Colleges (2014)
